Show HN: Convert Anthropic and OpenAI bill exports to FinOps FOCUS (open source)
items.summary: I needed to put our Anthropic and OpenAI spend next to our cloud bills, and found that the exports don't fit together. The Claude Console gives you two CSVs. The Cost export has dollars rounded to the cent, so a day of cache reads shows $0.00. The Usage export has token counts and no dollars. Anthropic also counts input in four parts that don't overlap: uncached, cache reads, 5-minute cache writes and 1-hour cache writes, priced at 1×, 0.1×, 1.25× and 2× input. OpenAI does it differently: input_tokens already includes cached tokens. If you merge the two exports without accounting for that, you double-count or drop cached input. FOCUS is the FinOps Foundation's open billing schema. AWS, GCP and Azure already export it, but the official converters don't cover any AI provider yet. So this is a small MIT CLI: npx ai-bill-to-focus convert cost.csv usage.csv -o focus.csv --check It writes one row per day, model and token type, each with its own SKU, unit price and quantity. The dollar column is always the provider's own figure. For Anthropic, a row gets the exact token-priced amount only if that rounds to the Cost export's cents; otherwise it keep and a column says which. check runs theFinOps Foundation's validator rules, which I ported to JS, and exits non-zero on errors, so it can gate CI. Rulecan't evaluate are counted and reported, n Status: Anthropic is tested on real Consolhe cent. OpenAI and Together AI are built from their documented export formats and haven't been run on a real file yet. If you have one and it breaks, theheader row alone is enough for me to fix i Network: convert downloads a public model the request contains nothing from your files. --offline skips it, and --prices lets you supply your own list. There's also an in-browser version that doesn't upload anything: https://www.cognocient.co I work on Cognocient AI, which does this kequest (by feature, team or agent run)through a proxy. The CLI works on its own with no account. I'd especially like feedback from anyone already loading FOCUS data into a warehouse.

Show HN: Ocel – Deploy apps to your AWS,GCP or VPS with infra from code
items.summary: Hey HN, I’m Victor and I’ve been building Ocel, an open source CLI, Console and SDK for deploying your apps and the infra they need to your own AWS/GCP/VPS. The CLI: Run ‘ocel deploy’ in your existing apps, and deploy to a configured target, no separate IaC files required. The SDK: Declare infra your app needs as code within the app itself, the CLI builds and provisions with no extra steps when deploying. Rust, Go, Python and Typescript supported. The Console: Optional self-hostable UI for an otherwise CLI-first product. The neat part is that the console itself is an app built with the sdk and deployed with the CLI ! You can try it out to deploy your apps to your own infra. VPS is well tested, and AWS+Cloudflare is also quite well covered. I’ve been dogfooding this myself for things I’m building. Please expect bugs, as it’s still early days. Why ? I’ve been a big fan and user of SST for a long time (personal and professional projects). The DX is genuinely unmatched and the high-level components make things quite easy. I think they proved that most apps don’t need complex IaC code, and abstracting things behind high level components/primitives, with some customization levers, actually works quite well. Ocel builds on that by taking it a bit further, no infra code, have a similar ‘high level components’ approach, but directly in the app. And support deploying existing apps or frameworks from day one in the CLI. You should be able to cd into an existing app and just deploy! (Of course theres a bit more like providing credentials to the platform you are deploying to, domains, one-time setup, etc). Everything else is the gripes I had after deploying tons of apps with SST: - Preview and production separation built in, so previews can share heavy resources and be considerably faster - First class support for separating the origin and edge, so composing AWS and cloudflare (common setup I had) becomes a breeze - CLI-first product, but with a UI console that can also be self hosted for things like team management, setting env vars, etc. - More SDK primitives (Realtime, Tasks, Pubsub topics, etc) that give a BaaS-like experience no matter where you deploy
